title: Workflows vs. agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: What single question tells you whether a part of your makerspace assistant is a workflow or an agent?

options.text: How many tools the system has to call
How many times the model gets called
Whether code or the model decides the next step
How large the model's context window is

items.stem: Your assistant answers manual questions by always retrieving the same section, then having the model write from it. Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: A workflow, because the code decides each step in advance
An agent, because the model still writes the final answer
An agent, because more than one step happens
A workflow only if no tool is ever used

items.stem: For a troubleshooting request, the model itself decides, call by call, whether to search the manual, ask a question, or check the calendar. One word: workflow or agent?
Your sponsor's model budget is small. For a step whose order never changes, which choice keeps the cost per request most predictable?

options.text: An agent, so the model can skip steps on its own
A fixed workflow, since code already knows each step in advance
A bigger model, since it finishes the task in fewer words
More tools, so the system finds the cheapest path itself

items.stem: In a few words, when is a fixed workflow the better choice over an agent, for keeping behavior and cost predictable?
Manual lookup in your assistant always runs the same fixed steps, but in the booking step the model itself decides what to check first. What is the overall system?

options.text: A pure agent overall, since the model decides something
A pure workflow overall, since most steps are fixed
Impossible to say without reading through all the code
A mix: workflow for one part, agent for another
